newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Two children survive Colombian jungle plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Two children survive Colombian jungle plane crash.

text.p: Two small children and their grandmother were rescued by helicopter on Monday from a jungle-covered area of northwest Colombia where their small commuter plane disappeared on last Thursday, authorities said.

A spokesman for the Civil Aviation Authority identified the survivors of the crash in a remote and guerrilla-infested area of Choco province as Leonardo and Carolina Aldana, ages 5 and 3 respectively, and Celia Palacio, the children's 60-year-old grandmother.
The children's mother, another women identified as a relative and the aircraft's pilot were all killed in the crash, the spokesman said. He said the cause of the crash was under investigation.
The children were severely dehydrated but in apparent good condition otherwise, the spokesman said, adding that the grandmother had suffered apparently serious injuries to one leg.

Earlier, the Civil Aviation Authority announced the discovery, in a mountainous area of neighbouring Antioquia province, of the wreckage of a small Cessna missing since Friday while searching for the plane that went down in Choco. All four people aboard the rescue aircraft were killed.
